cfn_corpus_scope.note: AWS intros target the CFN-registry corpus (sdk/providers/descriptions/aws.json, 1,437 resource types), scoped explicitly to exclude the 1,684-page HashiCorp corpus, which is being moved to aws-hashicorp/ and kept as-is rather than improved this phase. The 7 pre-existing hand-authored entries (aws_s3_bucket, aws_ecr_repository, aws_sqs_queue, aws_iam_policy, aws_iam_role, aws_iam_role_policy_attachment, aws_vpc) predate this scoping and are HashiCorp-named; they are left in place, not part of CFN batch counting below.

batches.note: Index 502 (aws_ecr_repository) already had a hand-authored intro from Phase 2 (identical CFN and HashiCorp name for this one resource); left untouched rather than overwritten, so this batch covers 99 of its 100 index range rather than 100.

intros.sourcing_notes: Batch 1 of the AWS CFN corpus (indices 0-96 of 1,437, alphabetically: aws_access_analyzer_analyzer through aws_app_test_test_case). 57 of 97 resources map to their own real, specifically-documented vendor concept (IAM Access Analyzer, AWS Private CA, Bedrock AgentCore Agent Registry, CloudWatch AIOps investigation groups, Amazon MQ brokers, AWS Amplify Hosting, Amplify UIBuilder, Amazon API Gateway REST APIs resources/stages/usage plans, AppConfig's full application/environment/deployment/experimentation surface, Amazon AppFlow, AppIntegrations, App Mesh's core mesh/node/router/service components, App Runner, WorkSpaces Applications (the renamed Amazon AppStream 2.0), AppSync GraphQL APIs and Events, and AWS Mainframe Modernization Application Testing). 40 are real, narrower scopes or association resources for a concept documented elsewhere in the same service (a usage-plan key against its usage plan, a v2 API Gateway sub-resource against the v2 API concept, an AppStream fleet/stack/entitlement association against the resource it associates, an AppSync API key or domain name against the GraphQL API it authorizes or fronts), the same parent-concept pattern proven across the prior five providers, most densely in this batch across API Gateway v1/v2's many sub-resources. 0 genuine skips: every one of the 97 real overview or reference pages fetched returned substantive content. Two notable non-recency findings surfaced live rather than assumed: AWS App Mesh carries an end-of-support notice (discontinued September 30, 2026, in favor of Amazon ECS Service Connect) and AWS App Runner is no longer open to new customers, both real, current vendor-page facts folded into their own intros rather than written as if the services were in normal active growth. Amazon AppStream 2.0 was verified live to have been renamed Amazon WorkSpaces Applications, with a real, newly expanded concepts page (agent sessions, computer use, an MCP service for AI agents) alongside its original fleet/stack/image-builder/app-block model; directory_config and entitlement, absent from that renamed concepts page, were confirmed real and still documented via a second, more targeted search rather than being assumed stale or skipped, the same two-search minimum the ticket's own GCP rollout_plan precedent established. No paid API used; all research and writing done locally this session (WebSearch/WebFetch + direct authoring). Next batch starts at CFN index 97 (aws_application_auto_scaling_scalable_target). Batch 2 (indices 97-196 of 1,437, alphabetically: aws_application_auto_scaling_scalable_target through aws_certificate_manager_certificate). 80 of 100 resources map to their own real, specifically-documented vendor concept, spanning Application Auto Scaling, Application Insights, Application Signals, Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, ARC Region switch and zonal autoshift, Athena, Audit Manager, EC2 Auto Scaling and Auto Scaling Plans, AWS B2B Data Interchange, AWS Backup (including its Audit Manager sub-feature, legal holds, air-gapped vaults, and restore testing), AWS Batch (including 2025's consumable-resource scheduling and SageMaker service environments), AWS Billing and Cost Management's newer BCM Dashboard/Pricing Calculator/Data Exports surface, Billing Conductor, custom billing views, Amazon Braket, AWS Budgets, the entire Amazon Bedrock core surface (agents, knowledge bases, guardrails, automated reasoning checks, flows, prompt management, inference profiles, intelligent prompt routing, sessions, data automation), the entire Amazon Bedrock AgentCore surface (runtime, memory, gateway with rate limiting, identity/OAuth2, browser and code interpreter tools, harness, evaluations, payments, capacity providers), Connect Cases, Amazon Keyspaces, Cost Explorer's anomaly detection and cost categories, and AWS Certificate Manager. 20 are real, narrower scopes or association resources for a concept documented elsewhere in the same service, most densely across Bedrock AgentCore's gateway sub-resources (target, rate limit, rule) and its dataset/evaluator pairing, and across AWS Backup's restore-testing plan/selection and framework/report-plan pairing. 0 genuine skips: every one of the 100 real overview or reference pages fetched returned substantive content. Bedrock's own core service page surfaced a real, current status finding rather than an assumption: Amazon Bedrock Agents (now Bedrock Agents Classic) is no longer open to new customers, superseded by Bedrock AgentCore, mirroring Batch 1's App Runner and App Mesh findings; AWS Audit Manager was independently confirmed to be in the same no-new-customers state. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore itself, along with roughly a third of this batch (Application Signals, AMP anomaly detection, ARC Region switch, Batch consumable resources and service environments, most of the BCM surface, Bedrock's automated reasoning checks, session management, and the entire AgentCore payments/harness/evaluations surface), are genuinely 2024-2026 features verified live via WebSearch, several from mid-to-late 2025 and 2026, well past the point memory alone would be reliable, the same discipline Kubernetes and GCP Compute established earlier in this phase. No paid API used; all research and writing done locally this session (WebSearch/WebFetch + direct authoring). Next batch starts at CFN index 197. Batch 3 (indices 197-296 of 1,437, alphabetically: aws_chatbot_custom_action through aws_comprehend_document_classifier). 81 of 100 resources map to their own real, specifically-documented vendor concept, spanning AWS Chatbot, Amazon Chime SDK Identity and Messaging, AWS Clean Rooms and Clean Rooms ML, AWS Cloud9, the full CloudFormation registry surface (hooks, macros, custom resources, stack sets, type activation), an extensive real CloudFront surface including several newer additions (Anycast static IPs, VPC origins, mTLS trust stores and Connection Functions, continuous deployment, SaaS Manager distribution tenants, KeyValueStore), CloudTrail Lake, CloudWatch (including 2026's log alarms and alarm mute rules), CodeArtifact, CodeBuild, CodeCommit, CodeConnections, CodeDeploy, CodeGuru, CodePipeline, CodeStar's still-active Connections and Notifications sub-services, the entire Cognito user pool and identity pool surface, and Amazon Comprehend custom classification. 19 are real, narrower scopes or association resources for a concept documented elsewhere in the same service, most densely across Clean Rooms's association resources, Cognito's attachment resources (role, principal tag, user-to-group, regional configuration, UI customization), and the CodeStar Connections family sourced from its own current CodeConnections rename. 0 genuine skips. This batch surfaced the sharpest concentration yet of the two patterns flagged across the whole phase: four more services closed to new customers or in maintenance mode, on top of the four already found in Batches 1 and 2, AWS Cloud9 (closed July 25, 2024), AWS CodeCommit (closed July 25, 2024), Amazon CodeGuru Reviewer (maintenance mode, closed November 7, 2025), and AWS CodeStar itself (discontinued for new projects July 31, 2024, though its Connections and Notifications sub-services were explicitly unaffected and remain active under the CodeConnections rename), eight services total across three batches that would each have read as healthy, unremarkable services if written from memory instead of verified live. Several resources were also confirmed as genuinely 2024-2026 features via WebSearch rather than assumed, including CloudFront VPC origins (November 2024), Connection Functions and WebSocket support for VPC origins (2026), CloudWatch alarm mute rules (February 2026) and log alarms (July 2026), and Cognito's terms-of-use/privacy-policy documents (2025) and managed login branding. One naming trap avoided by looking rather than guessing: aws_cloud_front_connection_function reads like a nonsensical CFN-splitting artifact of 'CloudFront Function' but is a real, distinct, genuinely new 2026 resource type for mTLS handshake-time validation logic, confirmed only after a second, more targeted search past an initial guess that it might be a stale or malformed key. No paid API used; all research and writing done locally this session (WebSearch/WebFetch + direct authoring). Next batch starts at CFN index 297. Batch 4 (indices 297-396 of 1,437, alphabetically: aws_comprehend_flywheel through aws_deadline_queue_fleet_association). 58 of 100 resources map to their own real, specifically-documented vendor concept, spanning Comprehend flywheels, Compute Optimizer automation rules, the full AWS Config surface, an extensive real Amazon Connect contact-center surface (queues, routing, campaigns, the 2025 data table, workspace, and native testing features), Control Tower, Cost and Usage Reports, Site-to-Site VPN customer gateways, Connect Customer Profiles, AWS Glue DataBrew, AWS Data Exchange, AWS Data Pipeline, AWS DataSync, Amazon DataZone, DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX), and AWS Deadline Cloud. 42 are real, narrower scopes or association resources for a concept documented elsewhere in the same service, the densest concentration yet, dominated by DataSync's 10 non-S3 location types (all sibling storage-system integrations parented to location_s3 per this phase's established pattern for enumerated-but-not-individually-detailed integrations) and DataZone's own dense web of domain/project/environment-scoped resources. 0 genuine skips. The single most significant finding this batch: Amazon Connect's own welcome page states that "Amazon Connect" now names a broader portfolio of agentic business-function solutions, with the contact-center product these resources belong to renamed "Amazon Connect Customer" (or simply Customer) in AWS's own documentation, the two names used interchangeably during the transition, folded into aws_connect_instance's own intro rather than repeated across all 27 aws_connect_* resources. AWS Data Pipeline was confirmed closed to new customers since July 25, 2024, a ninth service closed, deprecated, or in maintenance mode found across four batches now, again a status that would have read as healthy from memory alone. Amazon Connect's own data table, workspace, custom metrics, and native testing/simulation capabilities, AWS Compute Optimizer automation rules, and Control Tower's baseline primitive were all confirmed as genuinely 2024-2025 features verified live rather than assumed stable, long-standing capabilities. No paid API used; all research and writing done locally this session (WebSearch/WebFetch + direct authoring). Next batch starts at CFN index 397. Batch 5 (indices 397-496 of 1,437, alphabetically: aws_deadline_queue_limit_association through aws_ec2_vpnconnection). 60 of 100 resources map to their own real, specifically-documented vendor concept, spanning the remainder of Deadline Cloud, Detective, the brand-new AWS DevOps Agent, DevOps Guru, Direct Connect, Directory Service, DLM, an extensive real DMS surface (including Schema Conversion and Serverless data migrations), DocumentDB and DocumentDB Elastic Clusters, Elastic Disaster Recovery, Aurora DSQL, DynamoDB, and a large, foundational slice of core EC2 networking (fleets, VPN, IPAM, Transit Gateway, Verified Access, Traffic Mirroring, Network Insights, Local Gateway, and several newer VPC controls). 40 are real, narrower scopes or association resources for a concept documented elsewhere in the same service, the densest concentration of any batch so far, dominated by EC2's own web of attachment, association, and entry resources (Transit Gateway's nine sub-resources, IPAM's six, Local Gateway's four, Client VPN's three, Traffic Mirroring's three), reflecting how EC2 networking is itself built from many small, individually CloudFormation-addressable pieces around a few central resources rather than one page's worth of concepts each needing independent verification. 0 genuine skips. AWS Directory Service Simple AD was confirmed live to have closed to new customers on July 30, 2026, a date now in the past as of this session, the tenth service found closed, deprecated, or in maintenance mode across five batches. A second identity-shift case, distinct from a closure, also surfaced and was handled the same way batch 4's Amazon Connect Customer rename was: AWS DMS Fleet Advisor is itself being discontinued (May 20, 2026) while DMS Schema Conversion, the actual real feature aws_dms_data_provider and aws_dms_migration_project belong to, remains the active, current DMS capability, distinguished explicitly in their own intros rather than the two being conflated. A striking number of resources this batch were confirmed as genuinely 2024-2026 features verified live rather than assumed long-standing EC2 primitives, including AWS DevOps Agent itself (preview December 2025, GA March 2026), VPC Encryption Controls (2025-2026, with a documented pricing transition date), Site-to-Site VPN Concentrator (November 2025), EC2 IPAM's prefix list resolver (2025), VPC Block Public Access exclusions (2024), Transit Gateway metering policies, EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint, and Verified Access, a reminder that even a mature, decade-old service like EC2 keeps shipping resources recent enough that writing from memory alone would risk describing them as older or more settled than they actually are. No paid API used; all research and writing done locally this session (WebSearch/WebFetch + direct authoring). Next batch starts at CFN index 497. Batch 6 (indices 497-596 of 1,437, alphabetically: aws_ec2_vpngateway through aws_fsx_file_system; 99 new entries written, since index 502, aws_ecr_repository, already carried a hand-authored intro from Phase 2 and was left untouched rather than overwritten). 47 of 99 resources map to their own real, specifically-documented vendor concept, spanning ECR, ECS (including November 2025's Express Mode and Managed Daemons), EFS, EKS (including November 2025's EKS Capabilities and 2023's Pod Identity), ElastiCache Serverless, Elastic Beanstalk, ELB, the legacy Elasticsearch/OpenSearch resource, the brand-new AWS Elemental Inference, EMR and EMR on EKS and EMR Serverless, AWS Entity Resolution, EventBridge and its Schema Registry, Amazon EVS, AWS FIS, AWS Firewall Manager, and FSx. 52 are real, narrower scopes or association resources for a concept documented elsewhere in the same service, again the majority of the batch, concentrated in ElastiCache's own cluster/parameter/subnet-group family, ELB's listener/rule/target-group chain, EventBridge's rule/destination/connection chain, and, distinctly this batch, the discontinued-service families (Evidently, Forecast, Fraud Detector) where every non-central resource was parented rather than independently researched once the service's own end-of-life was confirmed. 0 genuine skips. This was by far the heaviest batch yet for the closed/deprecated/discontinued pattern: Amazon CloudWatch Evidently was confirmed fully discontinued October 17, 2025 (not merely closed to new customers, the console and every Evidently resource are now inaccessible entirely, AWS pointing customers to AWS AppConfig instead); Amazon FinSpace closed to new customers October 7, 2025 with end of support dated October 7, 2026; Amazon Fraud Detector closed to new customers November 7, 2025; Amazon Forecast closed to new customers July 29, 2024; and the legacy AWS::Elasticsearch::Domain resource has been superseded by AWS::OpenSearchService::Domain since the service's own September 2021 rename to Amazon OpenSearch Service, four new closures plus one legacy-superseded resource in a single batch, bringing the running total to fourteen services now confirmed closed, deprecated, discontinued, or in maintenance mode across six batches. A distinction from Batch 5's DMS Fleet Advisor case was applied deliberately here: unlike a dying sibling feature inside a healthy service, Evidently, FinSpace, Forecast, and Fraud Detector are each the service the resource itself belongs to, so the deprecation note was warranted on every one of their resources, not just a central one, while still avoiding conflating an unrelated healthy resource with a dying one. Several resources were also confirmed as genuinely 2025-2026 features verified live, ECS Express Mode and ECR managed signing (November 2025), EKS Capabilities (November 2025), and AWS Elemental Inference itself (GA February 2026), a reminder that this pattern (service age is not a signal memory is safe) held for container and Kubernetes services just as it did for EC2 in Batch 5. No paid API used; all research and writing done locally this session (WebSearch/WebFetch + direct authoring). Next batch starts at CFN index 597.

last_migration.stopped_at: Migration complete for what exists: all 30,142 real entries from ubiquex/sdk/providers/descriptions/aws.json (CFN vendor + DeepSeek AI) plus the 7 hand-authored docs pages are in descriptions.json. Real gap, not a stopping point to resume from: 1,085 of the SDK artifact's 1,437 CFN-derived resource types (89.4% by count) use a naming convention (underscore-split CFN service names, e.g. aws_access_analyzer_analyzer) that does not match the live docs corpus's own HashiCorp-derived naming (aws_accessanalyzer_analyzer) -- only 352 resource types share a name. Next real onboarding session: decide whether AWS's docs corpus adopts CFN naming on its next regeneration (making the other 1,085 entries immediately usable) or whether a real alias/rename table is needed.
